info.name: Vachan API
info.description:
Phase 4 API (placement & gamification). Run the requests from top to bottom (folders 0 → 12) — each folder builds on the one before.

Login/Register automatically save the token into the collection variable `token`; every other request sends it as `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (collection-level auth).

Before you start: backend running (`npm run dev`), database migrated and seeded (`npm run db:migrate && npm run db:seed`).

request.description: 200 when API + database work; 503 when the database is down.
No token yet → 401 UNAUTHORIZED. (If you already logged in earlier, Postman may still hold a 'vachan_token' cookie for localhost — delete it under Cookies, or this returns 200.)
Creates an account and logs in. A new random email is generated each time (pre-request script).

exec: pm.test("No password hash in the response", () => pm.expect(JSON.stringify(json)).to.not.include("passwordHash"));

item.name: Register again with the same email (409)

request.description: Returns the user and a token. The token is saved automatically for the next requests.

item.name: 3. Languages & courses
item.description: Public content. The course detail shows YOUR lesson statuses when a token is sent.

exec: pm.test("Six courses, 16 lessons each", () => { pm.expect(json.courses.length).to.eql(6); json.courses.forEach(c => pm.expect(c.lessonCount).to.eql(16)); });

request.description: Lesson status: completed · current (started) · available (unlocked, not started) · locked.

exec: pm.test("First lesson available, the rest locked", () => { pm.expect(lessons[0].status).to.eql("available"); pm.expect(lessons.slice(1).every(l => l.status === "locked")).to.eql(true); });

item.name: Get course that does not exist (404)
4. Lessons
item.description: Lessons need a token. Answers are never sent to the browser.

exec: pm.test("No answers or explanations leak", () => { const t = JSON.stringify(json); ["isCorrect","correctPosition","explanation"].forEach(s => pm.expect(t).to.not.include(s)); });

item.name: Get lesson that does not exist (404)

request.description: Body is optional. { "restart": true } starts the run over instead of resuming.

item.name: Course now shows the lesson as current
5. Exercise attempts & resume (lesson te-u1-l1)
item.description: Answer → feedback → leave → resume → complete → unlock.

item.name: Leave and come back: start again (resumes)
6. More lessons & answer types (te-u1-l2 → te-u1-l4)
item.description: Completes two lessons (matching included), then typed answers.

item.name: Typed sound — spaces ignored (" i i ")
7. Review (mistakes)
item.description: Open mistake = answered wrong and not yet answered right in a review.

exec: pm.test("2 open mistakes, newest first", () => { pm.expect(json.review.openMistakes).to.eql(2); pm.expect(json.review.mistakes.map(m => m.exerciseId)).to.eql(["te-u1-l4-e5","te-u1-l1-e1"]); });
pm.test("Shows your answer and the correct one", () => { pm.expect(json.review.mistakes[0].yourAnswer).to.eql("u"); pm.expect(json.review.mistakes[0].correctAnswer).to.eql("ii"); });

item.name: Answer a mistake in review mode
Get progress for an untouched lesson
9. XP, level, streak, hearts & daily goal
item.description: After folders 5–8 this learner has 68 XP (level 2), a 1-day streak, 4 hearts (2 wrong lesson answers, 1 fixed in review) and today's goal met. Day changes (consecutive / missed day) are tested with SQL — see docs/GAMIFICATION.md.

item.name: Answer correctly → rewards in the response

exec: pm.test("2 XP for a new correct answer", () => { pm.expect(json.rewards.xpEarned).to.eql(2); pm.expect(json.rewards.totalXp).to.eql(70); });

item.name: Change daily goal to intense (50 XP)
10. Achievements & recommendations
item.description: Badges unlock when a rule is met; recommendations explain which rule picked them.

exec: pm.test("Unlocked: first lesson, flawless, mistake mender, goal getter", () => ["first-lesson","perfect-lesson","mistake-mender","goal-getter"].forEach(c => pm.expect(by[c].unlocked).to.eql(true)));
pm.test("Unfinished lesson te-u1-l4 is recommended", () => pm.expect(json.recommendations.some(r => r.type === "unfinished-lesson" && r.action.lessonId === "te-u1-l4")).to.eql(true));
pm.test("Every item explains its rule", () => json.recommendations.forEach(r => pm.expect(r.reason).to.be.a("string")));

item.name: 11. Placement test (Hindi)
item.description: Transparent scoring: 3 questions per unit, pass = 2+ correct, start at the first unit not passed.

exec: pm.test("12 questions, 4 skills, no answers", () => { pm.expect(json.questions.length).to.eql(12); pm.expect(new Set(json.questions.map(q => q.skill)).size).to.eql(4); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(json)).to.not.include("isCorrect"); });

item.name: Get result → 'You are ready for Unit 3'

exec: pm.test("Recommended unit 3", () => { pm.expect(json.result.recommendedUnit).to.eql(3); pm.expect(json.result.message).to.eql("You are ready for Unit 3 — First words."); });
pm.test("Start at Unit 3, 8 lessons unlocked", () => { pm.expect(json.chosenUnit).to.eql(3); pm.expect(json.lessonsUnlocked).to.eql(8); pm.expect(json.startLessonId).to.eql("hi-u3-l1"); });

item.name: Hindi course: units 1–2 placed out, Unit 3 lesson 1 available
12. RAG knowledge base (Phase 5)
item.description: Retrieval only — no chatbot, no LLM. Needs `npm run rag:index -w backend` first. Requires login (run 1. Auth → Login or Register first). The first search after the server starts loads the embedding model (a few seconds).

item.name: Search — How do I say hello in Telugu? (language inferred)

exec: pm.test("Expected chunk in the top 3", () => { const top = json.results.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.id); pm.expect(top.some((id) => ["te/phrases#hello-namaskaaram", "course/te/vocabulary#course-vocabulary-greetings"].includes(id)), top.join(", ")).to.be.true; });

pm.test("Results carry metadata, source and relevance", () => { const r = json.results[0]; ["language","level","topic","skill","contentType","source"].forEach((k) => pm.expect(r.metadata).to.have.property(k)); pm.expect(r.reference).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(r.relevance.similarity).to.be.within(0, 1); pm.expect(r.relevance.score).to.be.a("number"); });

item.name: Search — What is this Telugu word? అమ్మ

exec: pm.test("Expected chunk in the top 3", () => { const top = json.results.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.id); pm.expect(top.some((id) => ["te/vocabulary#family-words", "course/te/vocabulary#course-vocabulary-family"].includes(id)), top.join(", ")).to.be.true; });

item.name: Search — beginner grammar concept (Telugu word order)

exec: pm.test("Expected chunk in the top 3", () => { const top = json.results.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.id); pm.expect(top.some((id) => ["te/grammar#word-order-subject-object-verb"].includes(id)), top.join(", ")).to.be.true; });
pm.test("Nothing harder than beginner in the top 3", () => json.results.slice(0, 3).forEach((r) => pm.expect(r.relevance.levelMatch).to.not.eql("harder")));

pm.test("Expected chunk in the top 3", () => { const top = json.results.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.id); pm.expect(top.some((id) => ["ta/vocabulary#food-and-drink", "course/ta/vocabulary#course-vocabulary-food-drink", "ta/examples#i-want-water"].includes(id)), top.join(", ")).to.be.true; });

pm.test("Expected chunk in the top 3", () => { const top = json.results.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.id); pm.expect(top.some((id) => ["hi/verbs#past-tense-with-ne-the-ergative"].includes(id)), top.join(", ")).to.be.true; });

item.name: Search — out of scope (should be insufficient)
13. AI tutor (Phase 6)
item.description: RAG-grounded tutor. Needs: `npm run rag:index -w backend` and an LLM key in backend/.env (GEMINI_API_KEY, or LLM_PROVIDER=groq + GROQ_API_KEY) — check with `npm run ai:check -w backend`. Log in first (folder 1). Rate limit: 6 tutor questions per learner per minute — if you get 429, wait a minute.

exec: pm.test("Tutor available (else see json.status.reason)", () => pm.expect(json.status.available, json.status.reason).to.be.true);
pm.test("Cites at least one retrieved note", () => pm.expect(answer.references.filter((r) => r.used).length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test("The hello note was retrieved", () => pm.expect(answer.references.map((r) => r.id)).to.include("te/phrases#hello-namaskaaram"));

item.name: Ask — follow-up in the same conversation

exec: pm.test("Previous question used for retrieval", () => pm.expect(answer.context.retrievalQuery).to.include("hello in Telugu"));
pm.test("Says it is not in the notes", () => pm.expect(answer.status).to.eql("insufficient"));
pm.test("The LLM was NOT called", () => pm.expect(answer.model).to.eql(null));
pm.test("No note was used", () => pm.expect(answer.references.filter((r) => r.used).length).to.eql(0));
pm.test("No LLM call, no retrieval", () => { pm.expect(answer.model).to.eql(null); pm.expect(answer.references.length).to.eql(0); });

item.name: Ask — why is my answer wrong? (exercise answered in folder 5)
14. Speech — listening & speaking (Phase 7)
item.description: Text-to-speech, speech-to-text and the speaking exercise. **Audio uploads are multipart/form-data** with the file in the field `audio` (WAV). The sample files are in `postman/audio/`; in the Postman app either set *Settings → General → Working directory* to the `postman` folder, or click each `audio` field and choose the file again. Postman cannot record from a microphone — use the app for real speech, or save the TTS audio (Send and Download) and upload it. Needs GEMINI_API_KEY (check: `npm run speech:check -w backend`). Rate limit: 10 transcribe/evaluate requests per minute.

request.description: What is configured on the server. Never contains API keys.

item.name: Play phrase: TTS for a course word (WAV)

request.description: Returns WAV audio of నమస్కారం. In Postman use **Send and Download** (arrow next to Send) to save it as a .wav file — you can upload that file to /speech/transcribe as a real-speech test. First call generates the audio (Gemini TTS), later calls come from the database cache (header X-Audio-Source).

item.name: Play phrase: TTS for a short text

request.description: Any short text (max 200 characters) in a course language — used for conversation lines.

**Body → form-data**: key `audio` (type File) + text fields `language`, `source`.

The sample file is a voice-LIKE test signal, not real speech: with real Gemini the transcript may be empty → 422 NO_WORDS_HEARD. For a real test, upload a WAV you recorded (or saved from the TTS request). With STT_PROVIDER=mock the transcript is the language's word for hello.

Expected phrase = course word te-v16-hello (నమస్కారం). Or send `expectedText` (+ `romanization`, `meaning`) instead of `vocabularyItemId`. Returns three separate parts: content (transcript vs phrase), pronunciation (AI notes — experimental, or not supported) and fluency (timing).

exec: pm.test("Pronunciation is separate (AI notes or not supported)", () => pm.expect(json.pronunciation.supported).to.be.a("boolean"));

item.name: Phrases to practise (with my best score)

exec: pm.test("Attempts (no audio stored)", () => { const a = pm.response.json().attempts; pm.expect(a).to.be.an("array"); if (a[0]) pm.expect(a[0]).to.not.have.property("audio"); });

request.description: Saves the first question's token in {{listeningToken}}.

exec: pm.test("Questions with 4 options, answer hidden", () => { pm.expect(q.length).to.eql(4); pm.expect(q[0].options.length).to.eql(4); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(q)).to.not.include("te-v"); });

pm.test("Correct? + the right option + the phrase", () => { pm.expect(json.correct).to.be.a("boolean"); pm.expect(json.correctChoiceId).to.match(/^[a-d]$/); pm.expect(json.answer.script).to.be.a("string"); });

item.name: 15. Conversation role-play (Phase 7)
item.description: Scenario role-play with an AI partner grounded in course vocabulary + RAG notes (needs `npm run rag:index -w backend` and GEMINI_API_KEY). Rate limit: 8 starts/replies per minute.

request.description: Saves the session id in {{roleplayId}}. The partner's line is based on the course vocabulary and the RAG notes for the scenario (turn.references).
Voice replies are two steps: POST /speech/transcribe (the learner checks the transcript), then this request with inputMode=voice and facts about the recording.

item.name: Reply: prompt injection → refused, no AI call

exec: pm.test("AI review or a note why not", () => pm.expect(s.summary.review || s.summary.reviewNote).to.be.ok);
